title: Rolling things down slopes
keyIdea: Prop a board on books and you have a ramp, a slope. Let go of a ball or a toy car at the top and the Earth pulls it down. Round things roll. Things with flat sides stay put or slide. Add more books and the slope gets steeper, so the car goes faster and further across the floor. A fair test changes only one thing: same car, more books.

kid: Put a board on some books. Now it is a slope, like a slide.
Let go of a ball at the top. Down it rolls! A car with wheels rolls too. A brick has flat sides. It stays put.
A tin can is round. But stand it on its flat end and it does not roll. Lay it on its curved side and away it goes.
Add more books. The slope is steeper now. The car goes faster and rolls further on the floor.
adult: In England, Development Matters (2023) asks 3 and 4 year olds to explore how things work and to explore and talk about forces they can feel, and Reception children to talk about the differences between materials and the changes they notice. In the US, kindergarten standards K-PS2-1 and K-PS2-2 ask children to compare how different pushes change an object's motion and to test a design that changes an object's speed or direction. A ramp is the classic first investigation for both.

The science, in words to use with your child: gravity pulls things down the slope. Round things (a ball, a wheel, a can on its side) touch the slope at one line or point and turn over and over, so they roll. Things with flat faces (a brick, a book, a sponge) grip the board and stay, or slide if the slope is very steep. A steeper slope means the car starts higher, so it is going faster at the bottom and rolls further before the floor slows it down.

Common mistakes to listen for: thinking heavy things roll and light things do not (shape decides it, not weight); thinking anything round always rolls (a can standing on its flat end stays put); and thinking a gentler slope is faster because it is longer. Be careful to keep it a fair test: use the same car, let go from the very top without a push, and change only the number of books.

In the lab your child stacks books and lets the car go from different heights, with a flag showing where each run stops; tests five toys to see which roll; tips a tin can, a kitchen roll and a crayon onto their sides; races a steep ramp against a gentle one; and picks the slope that stops the car by a teddy. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Lean a tray or a big book on a cushion and roll a toy car down it. Mark where it stops with a sock. Add a second cushion and try again. Ask: did it go further? Then try a ball, a block and a cup lying on its side.

visual.caption: Rolls or stays? Drag each card to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: tin can on its flat end

lab.caption: Flagship lab: stack books to make the slope steeper, test which toys roll, tip a can onto its side, race two ramps, stop by a teddy.

practice.prompt: Sam lets go of a ball and a brick at the top of a slope. Which one rolls down?
practice.hint: Think about shape. Which one is round all the way round?
practice.explain: The ball is round, so it rolls. The brick has flat sides, so it stays put.

practice.prompt: A ramp sits on {n} books. Mia adds 1 more book to make it steeper. How many books now?
practice.hint: Start at {n} and count on 1 more book.
practice.explain: {n} books and 1 more make {=n+1} books. The slope is steeper, so the car will go further.

practice.prompt: Ana wants her car to go further. What should she do to the ramp?
practice.hint: Think of the race. Which ramp sent its car further?
practice.explain: A steeper slope makes the car go faster, so it rolls further across the floor.

practice.prompt: Leo tests {n} balls and {k} bricks on a slope. Only the round ones roll. How many things roll?
practice.hint: Bricks have flat sides. Count only the balls.
practice.explain: Only the {n} balls roll, because they are round. The {k} bricks stay put, so {=n} things roll.

pool.prompt: Which ramp makes a toy car go fastest?
pool.hint: Which ramp had the most books under it in the race?
pool.explain: The steepest ramp makes the car go fastest, so it also goes furthest on the floor.

pool.prompt: A tin can stands on its flat end at the top of a slope. What happens?
pool.hint: Is it touching the slope with its round side or its flat end?
pool.explain: On its flat end it stays put. Lay it on its curved side and it rolls.

pool.prompt: Which of these will roll down a slope?
pool.hint: Look for the one that is round, with no flat sides.
pool.explain: An orange is round, so it rolls. A book and a sponge have flat sides, so they stay.

pool.prompt: A big heavy brick and a small light ball sit on a slope. Which one rolls?
pool.hint: Does weight decide, or does shape decide?
pool.explain: Shape decides. The ball is round, so it rolls, even though it is light. The brick stays.

pool.prompt: The car stopped before the teddy. How can you make it reach the teddy?
choices: Add a book to make it steeper
pool.hint: Steeper sends the car further. Gentler stops it sooner.
pool.explain: Add a book. A steeper slope makes the car go faster, so it rolls further to the teddy.

pool.prompt: A ramp sits on {n} books. You take 1 book away. How many books are left?
pool.explain: {n} books take away 1 leaves {=n-1}. The slope is gentler, so the car stops sooner.

pool.prompt: A car rolls {n} big steps from a low ramp. From a steeper ramp it goes 2 steps further. How far now?
pool.hint: Start at {n} and count on 2 more steps.
pool.explain: {n} steps and 2 more make {=n+2} steps. The steeper ramp sent the car further.

pool.prompt: You want a fair test of slopes. What should you change?
pool.hint: If you change the car too, can you tell which change made the difference?
pool.explain: Change only the books and keep the same car. Then you know the slope made the difference.
